disposition_mapping.rationale: Document retrieval is mechanical and carries no decision content; it becomes an event-triggered, automated retrieval sub-function inside TS-01 rather than a human-paced, separately staffed step. It is unconstrained_by_design, so no requirement forces its survival as a discrete step, but the assembled document set is still produced and remains independently retrievable, preserving the evidential chain back to the three source documents.

Quantity comparison runs inside the same automated pass as retrieval and price matching (TWM-R-01), but is preserved as a separately named, independently retrievable output (quantity variance detail) rather than being folded into an opaque single match flag, and continues to consume GRN data directly (TWM-R-03). Keeping it a distinct output, not a distinct human-staffed step, lets the function survive while removing a non-decision-bearing handoff.

Price/terms comparison is deterministic, rule-expressible work that runs in the same automated pass as quantity matching (TWM-R-02), continuing to consume PO data directly (TWM-R-04). Its output remains separately labelled from quantity variance, with any exchange-difference component kept separately identifiable per the FX-tracking principle, so the merge compresses the step boundary without compressing the evidence.

Tolerance evaluation survives as a distinct step, not folded into TS-01, because it depends on a governed, versioned policy artifact with its own change-control cadence rather than on transactional documents; keeping it separate preserves an audit seam (which policy version fired, on which invoice) that a merge into the matching pass would hide. The tolerance policy remains an explicit, versioned input (TWM-R-05/06), now applied under a federated governance model (centrally governed bands, locally selectable parameters) so constrained sites can operate it without unreviewed drift.

Exception investigation and resolution survives as the load-bearing human-judgment step in the redesign (TWM-R-10): an assistive agent may pre-assemble evidence and propose a disposition, but the accept/correct/reject decision and its documented basis remain an accountable human act, consistent with the council's unanimous refusal to automate this function. Restructuring reflects richer tooling (evidence packets, root-cause taxonomy) around an unchanged accountable actor.

Release approval survives (TWM-R-07) but is restructured into a tiered gate: clean, in-tolerance, no-exception-history matches auto-release through a deterministic logged policy engine, since no incremental judgment exists beyond TS-02's classification, while every exception-touched or override case still requires explicit human supervisor approval. Exception resolution (TS-03) precedes release in all cases (TWM-R-08), and the supervisor is never the TS-03 actor, with a named mechanism specified for thin-staffed sites (TWM-R-09).

Control reporting survives but moves from periodic batch compilation to continuous, event-driven logging of match outcomes, overrides and policy versions, which catches drift while it is still cheap to intervene. A periodic, named-reviewer-attested match-rate and override report is retained on top of that continuous record so that evidence of control is not just present in the system but demonstrably reviewed by an accountable person, satisfying the evidential-trail concern raised across the council.

steps.actor: Matching automation (retrieval and comparison agent/engine), with AP analyst as fallback executor and exception-queue recipient on stall
steps.description: An event-triggered matching agent fires automatically once an invoice is validated: it retrieves the linked PO and GRN from the ERP, then executes line-level quantity comparison against the GRN and price/terms/tax comparison against the PO in a single automated pass. The two comparisons are internally sequenced so that a failed or incomplete precondition (e.g. GRN retrieval failure, unparseable PO line) causes that comparison to stall and escalate rather than letting a downstream comparison silently proceed on an incomplete document set. The step always emits three separately named, independently retrievable artifacts rather than a single opaque match flag: the assembled document set, quantity variance detail, and price/terms variance detail (with any FX/exchange-difference component of a price variance held as a separately identifiable field, never blended into the variance figure). Under system outage or unreliable connectivity, the function degrades to a documented fallback: queued/batched processing against a local staging extract, or manual matching by an AP analyst using the same three source documents; missing or ambiguous data is queued and flagged as insufficient, never defaulted to a pass.
steps.name: Automated match execution
outputs: Price and terms variance detail (with exchange-difference component separately identifiable)

steps.actor: Tolerance rules engine (automated application); tolerance policy owner (accountable for policy content and version governance, not for per-invoice classification)
steps.description: Quantity and price/terms variance detail are evaluated by a deterministic rules engine against the current approved, versioned tolerance policy, producing a match classification (clean, tolerance, or exception) that explicitly references the policy version applied. This remains a distinct function and step from TS-01 because it depends on a governed configuration artifact with its own change-control cadence, not on transactional documents regenerated per invoice; collapsing it into the matching pass would make the policy basis for acceptance invisible except in its downstream effect, which is an assertion, not a control. The tolerance policy itself is a centrally versioned and change-controlled artifact with locally selectable parameters within centrally governed bands, so constrained sites can operate it without a central change request while drift is prevented; every applied version is logged. Any variance the engine cannot classify with confidence defaults to escalation into the exception queue, never to automatic clearance.
inputs: Tolerance policy (versioned, centrally governed with locally parameterized bands)
steps.name: Automated tolerance evaluation and classification
outputs: Match classification (clean, tolerance or exception), referencing applied tolerance policy version

steps.description: Matches classified as exceptions route to a named, accountable AP analyst, ideally a concentrated exception-investigation specialist rather than diffuse generalist capacity, as matching/comparison labour is automated. An assistive agent pre-assembles an evidence packet (source documents, vendor correspondence, prior resolutions for the same vendor/part, a root-cause taxonomy) and may propose a candidate disposition, but the agent never auto-applies a resolution: the analyst must affirmatively construct or select the accept/correct/reject decision and document its basis. Where the evidence packet itself is deficient (incomplete GRN detail, missing correspondence), the analyst escalates further or resolves with an explicit data-quality caveat rather than treating gaps as resolved. Organisations automating TWM-01-03-equivalent matching work name an explicit reskilling path for displaced generalist analysts into this specialist role and into data-quality remediation and vendor liaison.
inputs: Agent-assembled evidence packet (vendor correspondence, prior resolutions, root-cause taxonomy)
steps.name: Exception investigation and resolution (human-led, agent-assisted)

steps.actor: Automated release gate (logged policy engine) for clean/in-tolerance no-exception matches; AP supervisor (distinct from the TS-03 actor) for exception-touched or override matches
steps.description: Matches that are clean or within tolerance and carry no exception history and no override release automatically through a deterministic, logged policy-engine gate: this applies the risk appetite already encoded in TS-02's classification and introduces no new judgment, so it is a legitimate automation target rather than a ceremonial checkpoint. Any match that has touched exception resolution, carries a tolerance override, or is ambiguous/incompletely classified is routed to a human AP supervisor who reviews the full resolution evidence from TS-03 (not merely a pass/fail flag) before authorising release. The supervisor is never the same individual who resolved the exception in TS-03; at thin-staffed AP functions this separation is enforced by a named concrete mechanism (rotation, a second-site reviewer, or a dual-control checklist), not asserted as a role-matrix line item alone. Exception resolution (TS-03) always precedes release authorisation for any item that was exception-classified; ambiguous cases default to the human lane, never to auto-release.
steps.name: Tiered match release approval
outputs: Released match authorisation (lane-tagged: automated or supervisor-approved)

steps.description: Match outcomes, tolerance overrides, applied policy versions, and exception resolutions are logged continuously and immutably as they occur, rather than compiled after the fact, surfacing override concentration by approver and by vendor so the accountability created in TS-03/TS-04 remains checkable. A periodic match-rate and override report is generated from this continuous record and is reviewed with a named, dated sign-off by the AP accountant: continuous logging is the evidentiary mechanism, but a dashboard nobody attests to is a control gap in the other direction, so the governance act of a named person reviewing override and exception patterns at a defined cadence is retained on top of the continuous feed. A lightweight periodic batch extract remains an acceptable, non-degraded implementation of this function at sites without continuous BI tooling.
steps.name: Continuous match control logging and periodic attested review
outputs: Match-rate and override report with named reviewer attestation
